points.title: 早年生活
points.description: 约翰内斯·古腾堡出生于美因茨的一个富裕家庭，他的父亲富格尔是当地一位成功的商人。古腾堡年轻时接受了良好的教育，可能学习了金匠和宝石切割技术，这些技能后来对他发明活字印刷术至关重要。1420年左右，他离开美因茨前往斯特拉斯堡，开始了他早期的职业生涯，在那里他可能已经开始探索印刷技术。
points.descriptionEn: Johannes Gutenberg was born into a wealthy family in Mainz, where his father Fust was a successful merchant. Gutenberg received a good education in his youth, likely learning goldsmithing and gem-cutting techniques, which would later prove crucial to his invention of movable type. Around 1420, he left Mainz for Strasbourg, beginning his early career where he may have already begun exploring printing techniques.

points.title: 技术探索期
points.description: 在斯特拉斯堡期间，古腾堡开始了他对印刷技术的实验。他可能在这里开发了他的金属活字铸造技术，并尝试制造镜子和其他金属制品以资助他的研究。1434年至1444年间，他与安德reas Dritzehn合作，秘密进行印刷实验，开发出一种适合大规模印刷的金属合金和油墨配方。这一时期的技术积累为他后来回到美因茨并取得突破性进展奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: During his time in Strasbourg, Gutenberg began his experiments with printing technology. He likely developed his metal type-casting techniques here and attempted to produce mirrors and other metal products to fund his research. Between 1434 and 1444, he collaborated with Andreas Dritzehn, secretly conducting printing experiments and developing a metal alloy and ink formula suitable for mass printing. This technological accumulation laid the foundation for his later breakthrough upon returning to Mainz.

points.title: 印刷术革命
points.description: 回到美因茨后，古腾堡与富格尔合作，建立了历史上第一个印刷作坊。1450年左右，他完成了活字印刷术的关键发明，包括金属活字铸造技术、油墨配方和印刷机的设计。1455年，他完成了举世闻名的《古腾堡圣经》，这是西方世界使用活字印刷术印刷的第一本完整书籍，标志着印刷术革命的开始。这一发明彻底改变了知识传播的方式，为文艺复兴和宗教改革奠定了物质基础。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Mainz, Gutenberg partnered with Johann Fust to establish the first printing workshop in history. Around 1450, he completed his key inventions of movable type, including metal type-casting techniques, ink formulas, and printing press design. In 1455, he completed the renowned Gutenberg Bible, the first complete book printed in the Western world using movable type, marking the beginning of the printing revolution. This invention completely transformed the way knowledge was spread and laid the material foundation for the Renaissance and Reformation.

points.title: 法律纠纷与事业挫折
points.description: 1455年，古腾堡与富格尔之间爆发了法律纠纷，富格尔起诉古腾堡未能按时偿还贷款并要求获得印刷设备的所有权。法院判决富格尔胜诉，古腾堡失去了他的印刷作坊和大部分设备。尽管遭遇这一重大挫折，古腾堡并未放弃。他获得了美因茨大主教的资助，于1459年左右建立了新的印刷作坊，并继续印刷各种书籍，包括《古腾堡圣经》的简化版《三十六行圣经》。
points.descriptionEn: In 1455, a legal dispute erupted between Gutenberg and Fust, who sued Gutenberg for failing to repay loans on time and demanded ownership of the printing equipment. The court ruled in favor of Fust, and Gutenberg lost his printing workshop and most of his equipment. Despite this major setback, Gutenberg did not give up. He received funding from the Archbishop of Mainz and established a new printing workshop around 1459, continuing to print various books, including a simplified version of the Gutenberg Bible known as the 36-line Bible.

points.title: 晚年影响
points.description: 在生命的最后几年，古腾堡继续在美因茨从事印刷工作，虽然规模不如从前。1465年，美因茨大主教授予他终身年金，以表彰他对印刷术的贡献。古腾堡于1468年在美因茨去世，被安葬在当地的方济各会教堂。尽管他的晚年相对默默无闻，但他的发明已经产生了深远影响。印刷术的迅速传播使知识以前所未有的速度和广度传播开来，促进了欧洲的识字率提高、科学进步和宗教改革，彻底改变了人类文明的发展轨迹。
points.descriptionEn: In his final years, Gutenberg continued to work in Mainz, though on a smaller scale than before. In 1465, the Archbishop of Mainz granted him a lifetime pension in recognition of his contributions to printing. Gutenberg died in Mainz in 1468 and was buried in the local Franciscan church. Although his later years were relatively unremarkable, his invention had already had a profound impact. The rapid spread of printing allowed knowledge to be disseminated at an unprecedented speed and breadth, promoting increased literacy, scientific advancement, and the Reformation in Europe, completely altering the trajectory of human civilization.

appraisal.zh: 古腾堡被公认为现代印刷术之父，他将多种技术整合完善，创造出适合欧洲语言的金属活字印刷系统，使书籍成本大幅下降、知识得以广泛传播，为文艺复兴、宗教改革与科学革命奠定基础，其发明被视为近代史上最重要的技术革命之一。也有研究者指出他并非活字印刷的最初发明者，中国与朝鲜早有类似技术，其印刷最初多用于宗教文本，商业动机受到质疑，与合伙人的法律纠纷也反映商业利益与技术理想之间的冲突。
appraisal.en: Gutenberg is widely regarded as the father of modern printing: he integrated and perfected existing technologies into a metal movable-type system suited to European languages, sharply lowering the cost of books and spreading knowledge widely, laying foundations for the Renaissance, Reformation and Scientific Revolution, and his invention is counted among the most important technological revolutions of modern history. Yet some researchers note that he was not the original inventor of movable type, as China and Korea had earlier similar technologies; his printing initially served mainly religious texts, his commercial motives have been questioned, and legal disputes with partners reflected tensions between commercial interests and technological ideals.

supporter.zh: 古腾堡被誉为现代印刷术之父，他的发明彻底改变了人类知识传播的方式。活字印刷术的诞生使书籍生产成本大幅降低，知识不再局限于少数精英阶层，而是能够广泛传播。这一技术革命为文艺复兴、宗教改革和科学革命奠定了基础，推动了人类文明的进步。古腾堡的发明精神体现了人类对技术创新的不懈追求，他的遗产至今仍在影响着信息传播的方式。
supporter.en: Gutenberg is hailed as the father of modern printing, and his invention completely transformed the way human knowledge was disseminated. The birth of movable type dramatically reduced the cost of book production, allowing knowledge to spread widely rather than being confined to a small elite. This technological revolution laid the foundation for the Renaissance, Reformation, and Scientific Revolution, advancing human civilization. Gutenberg's innovative spirit embodies humanity's relentless pursuit of technological innovation, and his legacy continues to influence how information is transmitted today.

critic.zh: 批评者指出，古腾堡并非完全原创的发明者，而是整合和改进了已有的技术。在他之前，中国已经发明了活字印刷，朝鲜也有类似的印刷技术。此外，古腾堡的印刷术最初主要用于宗教文本，而非普及知识，其商业动机也受到质疑。他的发明虽然带来了知识传播的便利，但也加速了某些思想的传播，如宗教改革中的激进观点，这可能加剧了社会冲突。古腾堡的个人生活也充满争议，他与合作伙伴的法律纠纷反映了商业利益与技术理想之间的冲突。
critic.en: Critics point out that Gutenberg was not entirely an original inventor but rather integrated and improved existing technologies. Before him, China had already invented movable type, and similar printing technologies existed in Korea. Additionally, Gutenberg's printing was initially used primarily for religious texts rather than popularizing knowledge, and his commercial motives have been questioned. While his invention facilitated the spread of knowledge, it also accelerated the dissemination of certain ideas, such as radical views during the Reformation, which may have intensified social conflicts. Gutenberg's personal life was also marked by controversy, including legal disputes with business partners that reflected tensions between commercial interests and technological ideals.

objective.zh: 从历史客观角度看，古腾堡的发明是欧洲历史上的关键转折点，尽管他并非活字印刷的最初发明者。他的贡献在于将多种技术整合并完善，创造出适合欧洲语言的金属活字印刷系统。在流行文化中，古腾堡常被象征为创新者和变革推动者，他的故事体现了个人创新如何改变世界。历史学界普遍认为，印刷术的发明是近代史最重要的技术革命之一，其影响可与农业革命和工业革命相提并论。古腾堡的生平也反映了中世纪晚期向早期现代过渡时期的社会经济变革。
objective.en: From an objective historical perspective, Gutenberg's invention was a key turning point in European history, although he was not the original inventor of movable type. His contribution lay in integrating and perfecting various technologies to create a metal movable type printing system suitable for European languages. In popular culture, Gutenberg is often symbolized as an innovator and agent of change, with his story illustrating how individual innovation can transform the world. Historiography generally regards the invention of printing as one of the most important technological revolutions in modern history, its impact comparable to the Agricultural and Industrial Revolutions. Gutenberg's life also reflects the socio-economic transformations of the transition from the late Middle Ages to the early modern period.

self.zh: 科学和艺术是照亮人类前进道路的两盏明灯。
self.en: Science and art are the two lamps that illuminate the path of humanity.
